newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen surge in post-tankan trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen surge in post-tankan trade.

text.p: A widespread belief that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) was unlikely to hike rates given an unspiring tankan fuelled gains in SIMEX Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) and Euroyen futures on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Initial reaction in SIMEX was mild but JGBs shot up and hit their day's high, pulling along with them Euroyen and Nikkei," a dealer with a Japanese institution said.
Most believe there will be no change in BOJ policy and this helped JGBs and Euroyen, he added.
BOJ's morning injection of a net 200 billion yen into the market reinforced the belief of an accommodative BOJ stance.
On Wednesday, BOJ's tankan survey of corporate sentiment for November showed a limited improvement in business sentiment.
JGBs surged to their day's high after the tankan. Dealers said a fall in the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rate to an 11-month low of 0.50 percent fuelled the rally.
After hitting a high at 126.28, December JGBs ended up 0.72, at 125.98. Turnover was 495 lots.

Dealers said news that Japanese insurance funds were investing in Japanese bonds on top of foreign bonds, also underpinned JGBs. Support and resistance for December JGBs were at 125.00 and 126.50 respectively.
June Euroyen surged nine ticks from its IMM close to a high at 99.31. It was at 99.28 in late trade.
Some dealers said they were expecting Euroyen to post a mild technical correction towards 99.17, followed by a fall to 98.69 in the longer term.
Eurodollars were lacklustre amid thin interest ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
June ended at 94.44 against its IMM close at 94.44 on a turnover of 5,500 lots.
